## What this is, and what it is not

MR-Clust (Foley et al. 2021) treats each instrument's ratio estimate (its AD effect divided by its
T2D effect) as a draw from a mixture: a **null** cluster (no effect on AD), one or more **substantive**
clusters each with its own causal effect, and a **junk** component for outliers. It asks whether the
T2D variants split into groups that act on AD differently, without being told which groups to look
for.

Because the AD effects go into the clustering, this is **hypothesis-generating, not a test**: it
cannot be blinded, and any cluster it finds has been chosen by the outcome. The analysis plan fixed
two rules in advance, which are kept here:

- A degenerate solution (everything null) is acceptable and is reported as is, without tuning.
- The persuasive result would be **concordance**: MR-Clust membership lining up with the clusters
  defined without AD (Suzuki 2024), or with the KATP drug-target locus.

Instruments are the Xue 2018 set (109, the set used for the talk figures) and the Suzuki 2024 primary
set (273); outcome is SlopeHunter-corrected Bellenguez AD, with Kunkle as a check. Effects are on the
T2D risk allele; estimates are log-odds of AD per log-odds of T2D.

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

con_dir <- "results/pipeline/contrast"
snps <- read_csv(file.path(con_dir, "instrument_outcome_data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
xue_map <- read_csv(file.path(con_dir, "xue_cluster_map.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> select(SNP, suzuki = cluster)

# ---- settings: fixed before running ---------------------------------------------------------
runs <- tribble(~set, ~outcome, ~arm, ~label,
  "xue",     "ad_bellenguez", "slopehunter", "Xue instruments, Bellenguez (SlopeHunter)",
  "primary", "ad_bellenguez", "slopehunter", "Suzuki instruments, Bellenguez (SlopeHunter)",
  "xue",     "ad_kunkle",     "raw",         "Xue instruments, Kunkle",
  "primary", "ad_kunkle",     "raw",         "Suzuki instruments, Kunkle")
prob_cut <- 0.8      # a variant belongs to a cluster if its membership probability is at least this
min_size <- 4        # substantive clusters with fewer variants are reported but not interpreted
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theme_mc <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

run_mrclust <- function(set, outcome, arm, label) {
  d <- snps |> filter(.data$set == !!set, .data$outcome == !!outcome, .data$arm == !!arm) |>
    select(-any_of("cluster"))
  d <- if (set == "xue") left_join(d, xue_map, by = "SNP") else
    left_join(d, read_csv("assignments/instrument_assignments.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
                select(SNP, suzuki = cluster), by = "SNP")
  theta <- d$beta_y / d$beta_t2d
  theta_se <- d$se_y / abs(d$beta_t2d)            # first-order SE of the ratio estimate
  set.seed(20261028)
  fit <- mrclust::mr_clust_em(theta = theta, theta_se = theta_se, bx = d$beta_t2d, by = d$beta_y,
                              bxse = d$se_t2d, byse = d$se_y, obs_names = d$SNP,
                              plot_results = list("best", min_pr = 0.5))
  best <- fit$results$best
  list(label = label, data = d, best = best,
       assigned = best |> as_tibble() |> filter(probability >= prob_cut) |>
         select(SNP = observation, cluster, probability, cluster_mean, cluster_class))
}
fits <- purrr::pmap(runs, run_mrclust)
names(fits) <- runs$label
```

## Clusters found

```{r cluster-summary}
purrr::map_dfr(fits, \(f) {
  f$best |> as_tibble() |>
    group_by(cluster_class, cluster_mean) |>
    summarise(n_any = n(), n_assigned = sum(probability >= prob_cut), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(Run = f$label, .before = 1)
}) |>
  transmute(Run, Cluster = cluster_class,
            `Effect (OR per log-odds T2D)` = if_else(is.na(cluster_mean), NA_character_, sprintf("%.2f", exp(cluster_mean))),
            `Variants (any probability)` = n_any, `Variants (probability >= 0.8)` = n_assigned) |>
  kable(caption = "MR-Clust best-fitting solution per run (BIC-selected number of clusters)")
```

```{r cluster-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
plot_df <- purrr::map_dfr(fits, \(f) {
  top <- f$best |> as_tibble() |> group_by(observation) |> slice_max(probability, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |> transmute(SNP = observation, cluster_class, probability)
  f$data |> left_join(top, by = "SNP") |>
    mutate(cluster_class = if_else(probability >= prob_cut, cluster_class, "unassigned (p < 0.8)"),
           Run = f$label)
})
lines_df <- purrr::map_dfr(fits, \(f) f$best |> as_tibble() |> filter(!is.na(cluster_mean)) |>
                             distinct(cluster_class, cluster_mean) |> mutate(Run = f$label))
# Numbered clusters are relabelled by direction so a colour means the same thing in every panel.
sign_label <- function(cls, mean) case_when(cls %in% c("Null", "Junk") ~ cls,
                                            grepl("^unassigned", cls) ~ cls,
                                            mean > 0 ~ "Positive", TRUE ~ "Negative")
lines_df <- lines_df |> mutate(cluster_class = sign_label(cluster_class, cluster_mean))
plot_df <- purrr::map_dfr(fits, \(f) {
  top <- f$best |> as_tibble() |> group_by(observation) |> slice_max(probability, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    ungroup() |> transmute(SNP = observation, cluster_class = sign_label(cluster_class, cluster_mean), probability)
  f$data |> left_join(top, by = "SNP") |>
    mutate(cluster_class = if_else(probability >= prob_cut, cluster_class, "unassigned (p < 0.8)"), Run = f$label)
})
ggplot(plot_df, aes(beta_t2d, beta_y, colour = cluster_class)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70") +
  geom_abline(data = lines_df, aes(slope = cluster_mean, intercept = 0, colour = cluster_class), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = beta_y - 1.96 * se_y, ymax = beta_y + 1.96 * se_y), alpha = 0.3, width = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(plot_df, SNP == "rs5215"), aes(label = "rs5215 (KCNJ11)"),
                           colour = "black", size = 3.5, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ Run, scales = "free") +
  expand_limits(x = 0) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Positive = "#9A3324", Negative = "#2F65A7", Null = "grey55", Junk = "#A5A508",
                                 `unassigned (p < 0.8)` = "#FFCB05")) +
  labs(x = "Variant effect on T2D (log-odds)", y = "Variant effect on AD (log-odds)", colour = "MR-Clust cluster") +
  theme_mc
```

## Concordance with the clusters defined without AD

If MR-Clust found a real pathway-specific effect, its non-null clusters should be enriched for a
particular Suzuki cluster (for the Xue set, via the LD mapping in `xue_cluster_map.csv`). Fisher's
exact test of non-null membership against beta-cell membership:

```{r concordance}
purrr::map_dfr(fits, \(f) {
  a <- f$assigned |> filter(!grepl("Null|Junk", cluster_class, ignore.case = TRUE))
  d <- f$data |> mutate(non_null = SNP %in% a$SNP, beta_cell = grepl("^Beta cell", suzuki))
  tab <- table(factor(d$non_null, c(FALSE, TRUE)), factor(d$beta_cell, c(FALSE, TRUE)))
  ft <- if (sum(d$non_null) > 0) fisher.test(tab) else NULL
  tibble(Run = f$label, `Non-null variants` = sum(d$non_null),
         `of which beta-cell` = sum(d$non_null & d$beta_cell),
         `Beta-cell share overall` = sprintf("%d / %d", sum(d$beta_cell, na.rm = TRUE), nrow(d)),
         `Fisher OR` = if (is.null(ft)) NA else round(unname(ft$estimate), 2),
         `Fisher p` = if (is.null(ft)) NA else signif(ft$p.value, 2),
         `rs5215 cluster` = {
           r <- f$best |> as_tibble() |> filter(observation == "rs5215") |> slice_max(probability, n = 1)
           if (nrow(r)) sprintf("%s (p = %.2f)", r$cluster_class, r$probability) else "not in set" })
}) |> kable()
```

```{r non-null-members}
purrr::map_dfr(fits, \(f) f$assigned |> filter(!grepl("Null|Junk", cluster_class, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
                 left_join(f$data |> select(SNP, chr, pos, suzuki, beta_t2d, beta_y, p_2h, p_fg), by = "SNP") |>
                 mutate(Run = f$label, .before = 1)) |>
  transmute(Run, Cluster = cluster_class, SNP, chr, pos, `Suzuki cluster` = suzuki,
            `Membership p` = round(probability, 2), `T2D log-OR` = round(beta_t2d, 3),
            `AD log-OR` = round(beta_y, 3), `2 h glucose p` = signif(p_2h, 2), `Fasting p` = signif(p_fg, 2)) |>
  kable(caption = "Variants assigned (probability >= 0.8) to a non-null cluster")
```

## Reading the results

**Suzuki instruments: essentially degenerate, as the plan anticipated.** 259 of 273 variants sit in
the null cluster (218 confidently). A small positive cluster (OR 1.38 per log-odds T2D) has only one
confident member, rs76675804 at the *THADA* locus (beta cell +PI). rs5215 leans toward that cluster
but without confidence (membership probability 0.52). Kunkle finds nothing but the null cluster.

**Xue instruments: a split into positive and negative groups, not a pathway.** MR-Clust prefers three
components in SlopeHunter-corrected Bellenguez: a positive cluster (OR 1.18; 13 confident members),
a negative cluster (OR 0.82; 7 confident members) and a null cluster. rs5215 (KCNJ11) is a confident
member of the positive cluster (0.88), as is the *THADA* variant (rs17334919, the same locus as the
Suzuki result). But membership does not line up with the clusters defined without AD: the positive
cluster draws from every Suzuki cluster, and beta-cell variants are no more common in non-null
clusters than elsewhere (Fisher OR 0.96, p = 1.0). A symmetric split around a near-null average is
what MR-Clust tends to produce when single-variant ratios are simply more spread out than their
standard errors allow, so this is better read as heterogeneity than as two biological groups.

**The negative cluster is partly the MHC.** Two of its seven confident members are in the HLA region
on chromosome 6 (rs1063355, rs2246618), and rs1063355 is also the lead member of the only non-null
cluster in Kunkle. The other five (near *CDKAL1*, *GCKR*, *JAZF1*, *RBMS1* and on chromosome 22q13)
are established T2D loci with no obvious common thread. The HLA region carries its
own AD association (HLA-DR) and is routinely excluded from MR because of its long-range LD and
pleiotropy; MR-APSS in the main pipeline already drops it. These variants are best treated as
pleiotropic outliers.

**Concordance, the result the plan named as persuasive, is absent.** Neither run concentrates
beta-cell variants in a non-null cluster, and nothing replicates in Kunkle apart from the MHC variant.
The one consistent thread is rs5215 sitting on the positive side in both Bellenguez runs, which adds
nothing new to the fine-mapping result.

**Overall:** MR-Clust does not reveal a subgroup of T2D variants with a distinct effect on AD. This is
reported as is, without tuning, as fixed in the plan.
